title: Fix bugs in a Python singly linked list
description: Brownfield Python dirty_cleanup: fix three intentional bugs in a singly linked list (append adds to head instead of tail, length counts only first node, contains always returns False).

injections.content:
from src.linkedlist import LinkedList


def test_append_order():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.append(1)
    ll.append(2)
    ll.append(3)
    # head should be 1, then 2, then 3
    node = ll.head
    assert node.value == 1
    node = node.next
    assert node.value == 2
    node = node.next
    assert node.value == 3


def test_length():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.length() == 0
    ll.append(10)
    ll.append(20)
    assert ll.length() == 2


def test_contains_true():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.append(5)
    ll.append(10)
    assert ll.contains(10)


def test_contains_false():
    ll = LinkedList()
    ll.append(5)
    assert not ll.contains(99)


def test_empty_list():
    ll = LinkedList()
    assert ll.length() == 0
    assert not ll.contains(1)

task_spec.prompt:
Fix three bugs in src/linkedlist.py.

Bug 1 — append: prepends to head instead of appending to tail.
  Fix: traverse to the last node and set last.next = node. If head is None, set head = node.

Bug 2 — length: always returns 1 for non-empty lists.
  Fix: traverse all nodes counting each one.

Bug 3 — contains: never checks node.value, always returns False.
  Fix: add `if current.value == value: return True` before advancing current.

All 5 tests must pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: append adds nodes in insertion order (tail end)
length returns the count of all nodes
contains returns True if value exists, False otherwise
